# lifecycle: one task plan walked from `new` through every mutating command.
# IDs are deterministic: the harness sets AUTO_PLAN_SEED=1 and AUTO_PLAN_DATE=2026-01-01.

# expect exit=0 stdout=init.json
auto plan init
# expect exit=0 stdout=new.json
auto plan new demo --kind task
# checkpoint 1

# expect exit=0 stdout=add-goal.json
auto plan add 001 goal --title "Plans can be reordered without breaking references"
auto plan add 001 goal --title "An agent gets one stage's context in one call"
# expect exit=0 stdout=add-ac.json
auto plan add 001 ac --proves g-gc8t --title "brief is self-contained" --gwt "Given a stage, when brief runs, then its output needs nothing else" --verify-cmd "go test ./e2e -run Brief"
auto plan add 001 decision --title "brief is Markdown + JSON" --chosen "Markdown with --text, JSON by default" --why "agents read JSON; humans read Markdown" --by charlie
# checkpoint 2

# expect exit=0 stdout=link.json
auto plan link 001 d-kqxw constrains g-gc8t
# checkpoint 3

# expect exit=0 stdout=lint.json
auto plan lint 001
# expect exit=0 stdout=show.txt
auto plan show 001 --text

# update, a rejected alternative, a second AC, and an edge moved from the goal to the AC.
auto plan update 001 g-rbcw --description "Reordering rewrites one rank; no ID changes."
auto plan add 001 alternative --title "reuse Context Pack" --why "collides with auto-graph's term"
auto plan link 001 d-kqxw rejects a-w1fg
auto plan add 001 ac --proves g-gc8t --title "brief names no other stage" --gwt "Given two stages, when brief runs for one, then the other's steps are absent"
auto plan link 001 d-kqxw constrains ac-j58t
# expect exit=0 stdout=unlink.json
auto plan unlink 001 d-kqxw constrains g-gc8t
# expect exit=0 stdout=update.json
auto plan update 001 ac-j58t --verify-tests TestBrief --verify-tests TestBriefIsolated
# checkpoint 4

# A rejected write: rejects is decision → alternative, so an AC cannot start one.
# Exit 1, nothing on stdout, and graph.json stays byte-identical to checkpoint 4.
# expect exit=1 stdout=rejected.txt
auto plan link 001 ac-j58t rejects g-gc8t
# checkpoint 5

# expect exit=0 stdout=retire.json
auto plan retire 001 ac-bvmq
# expect exit=0 stdout=move.json
auto plan move 001 g-gc8t --before g-rbcw
# checkpoint 6

# expect exit=0 stdout=update-lifecycle.json
auto plan update 001 plan --lifecycle solution
# expect exit=0 stdout=fmt-check.json
auto plan fmt 001 --check
# checkpoint 7

# At solution, goal-no-ac applies: g-rbcw has no AC yet.
# expect exit=1 stdout=lint-solution.json
auto plan lint 001
# expect exit=0 stdout=show-solution.txt
auto plan show 001 --text

# renumber moves the plan to another number: folder 001-demo becomes 004-demo and the plan ID
# keeps its suffix (001-acs4 → 004-acs4). The bare number 001 then names nothing.
# expect exit=0 stdout=renumber.json
auto plan renumber 001 --to 004
# expect exit=1
auto plan lint 001
# checkpoint 8

# An annex: `add` writes a create-only stub `.md` beside graph.json and names it
# in the result (the `file` key / a `wrote …` line). The sidecar is diffed at the
# next checkpoint. The freeze below hashes every annex file into graph.json
# (annex.hash) — which is why the file must exist before `--lifecycle done`.
# (annex-changed, which fires once a frozen annex's bytes drift from that hash,
# needs a mid-scenario file edit the commands.txt harness has no primitive for;
# it is covered in internal/lint's unit tests, not here.)
# expect exit=0 stdout=add-annex.json
auto plan add 004 annex --kind usage --path demo-usage.md --title "Using demo"

# Setting lifecycle done is the plan's last write; afterwards it is frozen and writes are refused.
auto plan update 004 plan --lifecycle done
# expect exit=1 stdout=frozen.txt
auto plan add 004 goal --title "too late"
# expect exit=0
auto plan fmt 004 --check
# checkpoint 9
